Living on the Dead

By: Harri Vithi | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Unique Selling Point:
People building houses on graves

Summary:
Living on the Dead is the story of gross mismanagement of the Buffalo City Metro told through the decades long abandonment of several cemeteries by the municipality. In 2023, BCM was the leading contributor to irregular expenditure in the Eastern Cape at R 6.5 billion of R 10.6 billion total. Are the dead safe from corruption/mismanagement?

With cemeteries becoming the site of muggings, stabbings, druggies and now shacks - it appears not.


Further information:
Background
By 2015, cemeteries in the Buffalo City Metro were in an embarrassing state of disrepair.
https://www.pressreader.com/south-africa/daily-dispatch/20150309/281638188673012

Reports indicated visits made it difficult to tell whether these were abandoned stretches of land save for lone, random headstones here and there.

Never mind 10 years later, the municipality still hasn’t bothered to tend to the dead but perhaps that’s because it's struggling to manage the needs of the living.
https://www.dispatchlive.co.za/news/2024-01-15-run-down-cemeteries-are-a-hunting-ground-for-criminals/

The municipal crematorium is also a hot mess. Plaques on the wall of so-called remembrance are gone with ashes exposed. It’s assumed by some, the nyaope boys had the time of their lives smoking up the ashes of the forgotten.

It’s no wonder that, a week ago, reports began streaming in about a most bizarre turn of events - people building shacks atop and in around grave sites at Lujiza Cemetery.
https://www.news24.com/news24/southafrica/news/grave-invaders-east-london-families-exhume-loved-ones-due-to-cemetery-invasion-metro-neglect-20240827

In the ordinary course of business, there’s a sacred attachment to the places where the dead are buried. Spiritually, there may be consequences for desecrating a burial ground - not in BCM. Shacks and headstones have become very close neighbours.

Imagine children playing hide n’ seek amongst the few existing headstones - eerie, weird, bemusing…shocking.

Some distraught families of the departed have exhumed their bodies for reburial while others are making enquiries about the process. Seems it will cost R 30 000 and the municipality will be compelled to cover the cost given its failure to employ a basic monthly maintenance service and secure the properties.

The community man with a plan

Desperate families of the deceased have approached Lonwabo Yiliwe of the Eastern Cape Missing Persons Unit to help them gain access to their departed’s grave sites. It’s unclear whether this unit is attached to the police but their uniform certainly makes efforts to mimic the official SAPS one. Lonwabo says his legal department is in the process of securing eviction orders for the land invaders.

Lonwabo has promised to connect us with the families once we are in the Eastern Cape which is making things challenging. He is also quite difficult to get a hold of - often claiming to be busy. This has made it difficult to confirm case studies and I am still in the process of trying to secure other people on the ground who may be able to connect us with both the affected families and the grave dwellers.

Unanswered Questions

DA ward councilors - Shandre Hoffman and Lemarc Stewart sit on the Sports and Recreation portfolio committee in BCM (cemeteries fall under this portfolio). They are unable to advise when and why invaders decided the cemetery in Duncan Village would be a great place to build shelter but they believe it happened in the last few months.

Shandre and Lemarc say their questions about the state of cemeteries have gone unanswered for years. The response: we’ll get back to you. They say they only receive operational reports about the number of burials or cremations per month and nothing more.

Buffalo City Cemetery is in Ward 8, Duncan Village, it’s under councilor Kwanele Majeke.

Political Conspiracy Theories

Kwanele Zonke sits on the human settlements portfolio and he believes the land invasion is strategic. Kwanele says after this report on https://www.dispatchlive.co.za/news/2024-08-05-bcm-sits-for-two-years-on-siu-r21m-tender-abuse-report/
The report says:-
Allegations of gross financial misconduct relating to the provision of more than 330 temporary housing structures (THS) during the Covid-19 pandemic period, at a cost of R21m, are back to haunt six Buffalo City Metro officials who had been investigated by the Special Investigating Unit (SIU).

Kwanele believes there is a political hand that instructed the invaders to build shacks on the cemetery in order to create a disaster which would necessitate the release of funds. Whether his theory will hold remains to be seen.

Big monies, the usual promises

During Covid, the de-densification program promised to build 1174 TRU’s for Duncan Village. By 2022, the Special Investigation Unit reported to parliament that only 486 houses had been built at a cost of R75,653,734.00 (R64,441.00 per unit). (Un)surprisingly, the EC government deemed it logical to extend the contract with the errant providers for a further 3 months at an additional cost of R86,106,471.00 - this extension was deemed irregular by the Housing Development Agency. Furthermore, an engineer was paid a cool R 26 million to oversee construction of the units. The investigation also uncovered duplicate payments and collusion between government officials and the companies which won tenders. At the time they expected to recover a possible R112m.
Although the gravesite dwellers may not be beneficiaries of the de-densification units, there are multiple human settlement projects which have been at a standstill or delayed in the BCM for years. If BCM were meeting its housing targets, would we see people building dwellings atop the dead?

metadata.Summary: Living on the Dead is the story of gross mismanagement of the Buffalo City Metro told through the decades long abandonment of several cemeteries by the municipality. In 2023, BCM was the leading contributor to irregular expenditure in the Eastern Cape at R 6.5 billion of R 10.6 billion total. Are the dead safe from corruption/mismanagement? With cemeteries becoming the site of muggings, stabbings, druggies and now shacks - it appears not.
metadata.Further information: Background By 2015, cemeteries in the Buffalo City Metro were in an embarrassing state of disrepair. https://www.pressreader.com/south-africa/daily-dispatch/20150309/281638188673012 Reports indicated visits made it difficult to tell whether these were abandoned stretches of land save for lone, random headstones here and there. Never mind 10 years later, the municipality still hasn’t bothered to tend to the dead but perhaps that’s because it's struggling to manage the needs of the living. https://www.dispatchlive.co.za/news/2024-01-15-run-down-cemeteries-are-a-hunting-ground-for-criminals/ The municipal crematorium is also a hot mess. Plaques on the wall of so-called remembrance are gone with ashes exposed. It’s assumed by some, the nyaope boys had the time of their lives smoking up the ashes of the forgotten. It’s no wonder that, a week ago, reports began streaming in about a most bizarre turn of events - people building shacks atop and in around grave sites at Lujiza Cemetery. https://www.news24.com/news24/southafrica/news/grave-invaders-east-london-families-exhume-loved-ones-due-to-cemetery-invasion-metro-neglect-20240827 In the ordinary course of business, there’s a sacred attachment to the places where the dead are buried. Spiritually, there may be consequences for desecrating a burial ground - not in BCM. Shacks and headstones have become very close neighbours. Imagine children playing hide n’ seek amongst the few existing headstones - eerie, weird, bemusing…shocking. Some distraught families of the departed have exhumed their bodies for reburial while others are making enquiries about the process. Seems it will cost R 30 000 and the municipality will be compelled to cover the cost given its failure to employ a basic monthly maintenance service and secure the properties. The community man with a plan Desperate families of the deceased have approached Lonwabo Yiliwe of the Eastern Cape Missing Persons Unit to help them gain access to their departed’s grave sites. It’s unclear whether this unit is attached to the police but their uniform certainly makes efforts to mimic the official SAPS one. Lonwabo says his legal department is in the process of securing eviction orders for the land invaders. Lonwabo has promised to connect us with the families once we are in the Eastern Cape which is making things challenging. He is also quite difficult to get a hold of - often claiming to be busy. This has made it difficult to confirm case studies and I am still in the process of trying to secure other people on the ground who may be able to connect us with both the affected families and the grave dwellers. Unanswered Questions DA ward councilors - Shandre Hoffman and Lemarc Stewart sit on the Sports and Recreation portfolio committee in BCM (cemeteries fall under this portfolio). They are unable to advise when and why invaders decided the cemetery in Duncan Village would be a great place to build shelter but they believe it happened in the last few months. Shandre and Lemarc say their questions about the state of cemeteries have gone unanswered for years. The response: we’ll get back to you. They say they only receive operational reports about the number of burials or cremations per month and nothing more. Buffalo City Cemetery is in Ward 8, Duncan Village, it’s under councilor Kwanele Majeke. Political Conspiracy Theories Kwanele Zonke sits on the human settlements portfolio and he believes the land invasion is strategic. Kwanele says after this report on https://www.dispatchlive.co.za/news/2024-08-05-bcm-sits-for-two-years-on-siu-r21m-tender-abuse-report/ The report says:- Allegations of gross financial misconduct relating to the provision of more than 330 temporary housing structures (THS) during the Covid-19 pandemic period, at a cost of R21m, are back to haunt six Buffalo City Metro officials who had been investigated by the Special Investigating Unit (SIU). Kwanele believes there is a political hand that instructed the invaders to build shacks on the cemetery in order to create a disaster which would necessitate the release of funds. Whether his theory will hold remains to be seen. Big monies, the usual promises During Covid, the de-densification program promised to build 1174 TRU’s for Duncan Village. By 2022, the Special Investigation Unit reported to parliament that only 486 houses had been built at a cost of R75,653,734.00 (R64,441.00 per unit). (Un)surprisingly, the EC government deemed it logical to extend the contract with the errant providers for a further 3 months at an additional cost of R86,106,471.00 - this extension was deemed irregular by the Housing Development Agency. Furthermore, an engineer was paid a cool R 26 million to oversee construction of the units. The investigation also uncovered duplicate payments and collusion between government officials and the companies which won tenders. At the time they expected to recover a possible R112m. Although the gravesite dwellers may not be beneficiaries of the de-densification units, there are multiple human settlement projects which have been at a standstill or delayed in the BCM for years. If BCM were meeting its housing targets, would we see people building dwellings atop the dead?
